US Federal Reserve Holds Interest Rates Steady at 3.75% to 4% Amid Ongoing Inflation Concerns

29 Oct 2026, 10:06 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

Image: www.bbc.co.uk — Creative Commons

Key takeaways Fed Decisions and Current Policy Stand The US Federal Reserve has decided to keep interest rates steady at a target range of 3.75% to 4%. This announcement follows the central bank's decision to raise rates at its previous meeting in September—the first such increase

Fed Decisions and Current Policy Stand

The US Federal Reserve has decided to keep interest rates steady at a target range of 3.75% to 4%. This announcement follows the central bank's decision to raise rates at its previous meeting in September—the first such increase in three years. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh indicated that the earlier monetary adjustment is beginning to yield positive results, stating that "what we've done in this monetary medicine is starting to work some."

Despite holding rates steady this month, the central bank noted that inflation remains high. However, officials decided to pause further adjustments to gather additional economic data before determining future policy steps. While the broader economy continues to show resilience, policymakers acknowledged ongoing uncertainties and tightened credit conditions.

Dissension on the Committee

The decision to maintain the current rate was not unanimous among the policy committee. Ten of the twelve members voted in favor of keeping rates unchanged. In contrast, two officials—Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack—dissented, voting instead to raise the rate to a range of 4% to 4.25%.

When asked about potential rate movements at the committee's upcoming meeting scheduled for 8-9 December, Chair Warsh declined to commit to a specific trajectory, noting that incoming economic data over the coming weeks will provide a clearer picture.

Practical Implications and Reader Guide

What Rates Mean for Consumers

An interest rate determines the cost of borrowing money through credit cards, mortgages, or business loans, while also dictating the returns earned on cash savings. When the Fed holds rates steady:

  • Rates on new mortgages, car loans, and business loans are less likely to experience sudden shifts.
  • Returns on cash savings are unlikely to see immediate increases.

Confirmed Facts vs. Unknowns

  • Confirmed: The federal funds rate remains at 3.75% to 4%. Ten committee members voted to hold, while two voted for an increase. The next meeting is set for 8-9 December.
  • Unknown: Whether the central bank will raise, lower, or hold rates steady at the December meeting remains undetermined, as officials await further economic data.
